what_happened.line: The task force will ask a non-binding straw poll of town meeting to choose between a stormwater utility fee and continuing to fund stormwater work through the operating budget.
Members settled on billing every property a flat fee based on its impervious surface (an ERU approach) rather than tiered rates, if a utility is chosen.
Fees would be billed separately from the property tax bill, payable quarterly by tear-off coupon; municipal land would not be billed but churches and nonprofits would be.
A warrant article is due September 17, with two task force meetings around September 8 and 14 to draft and vote on its language before sending it to town counsel.
FinCom hears the proposal October 8, the Select Board October 20, and a public information session is planned around November 3, ahead of the November 17 special town meeting.

why_it_matters: Depending on which funding path town meeting favors in the non-binding vote, residents could see stormwater costs shift from the tax bill to a new separate utility bill tied to a property's paved and roofed area.
Churches, nonprofits and large commercial parcels would be billed under a utility approach even though they are often exempt from property tax, while town-owned land would not be billed.
The vote at town meeting is advisory only; the operating-budget alternative includes a stormwater engineer position that failed as an override once already.

minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force reviewed a detailed proposed stormwater utility budget (new engineer/GIS-manager hire, vendor costs for MS4 compliance sweeping and catch-basin cleaning, billing and indirect costs) that Bill plans to present to the Finance Committee, comparing it against the existing operating-budget storm water line and debating how much fee detail to disclose publicly. The group also reviewed a draft storm water utility bylaw, discussed governance options (an elected or appointed storm water commission), and set the schedule for FinCom, Select Board, a public information session, and the next task force meeting ahead of May town meeting.

what_happened.line: The task force agreed to split town meeting action in two: bring the storm water bylaw to the May annual town meeting first, and hold the fee and rate structure for a later special town meeting.
The draft bylaw and governance options -- a five-member elected board, a three-member elected board, or an appointed commission -- go to the Select Board ahead of its February 10 session.
The board set a run of dates: Finance Committee on February 5, Select Board on February 10, a public information session March 5, and the task force's own next meeting February 19.
The group leaned toward moving billing from quarterly to annual and looking at piggybacking it on the tax or sewer bill to cut postage costs.
No formal vote was taken on the budget or fee numbers; members debated at length how much fee detail to show the Finance Committee, without resolving it.

why_it_matters: This is the early groundwork for a new stormwater utility fee that would eventually appear as its own charge on property owners, separate from the tax rate itself.
Splitting the bylaw vote from the fee vote means the May town meeting decision on structure and governance would come before residents see a final rate or fee schedule.
How the bill is delivered -- annual versus quarterly, and whether it rides along with the tax or sewer bill -- affects when and how the charge shows up for a household.
